0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 February 1985, after the draft finahzetl by the Polishes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 It is a general practice in the shoe industry to give a hard, glossy transparent coating of a wax polish to the sole and edges of the finished boots, shoes, sandals, etc, for preservation and presentation value. Different manufacturers, both small and large, have evolved their own formulation and method of application. Polishing with a cake of beeswax alone or with a blend of beeswax is being practised even now, by some small manufacturers of leather footwears. 0.3 This standard was originally published in 1968. In this revision, non-volatile matter pH of water extract, distillation yield and flash point The requirement of iron content of volatile portion have been modified. has been deleted and a new characteristic `Keeping Quality' has been prescribed in this revision. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accorThe number of significant places retained dance with IS : 2-1960*. in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for the wax-solvent polish, natural or tinted, suitable for general application to soles and edges of leather footwear as finishes.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

IS : 4779 .. 1985 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this IS : 8171-1984* shall apply. 3. REQUIREMENTS shall be manufactured preferably 3.1 Description - The material with bleached waxe:, which when applied on sole and edges of footwear shall produce a transparent colourless wax film of sufficient hardness. 3.1.1 The material may be tinted slightly with oil agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 3.1.2 The material shall not have a disagreeable soluble colours as standard, the definitions given in

odour.

homogeneous and 3.1.3 Consistency - The material shall be smooth, It shall not flow at normal semi-solid mass, free from gritty material. temperature and shall have no tendency for the separation of solvents or crystallization of the constituted material when tested as prescribed in Appendix A. 3.1.4 Applicability and Drying Time - The polish shall not crumble or dry too rapidly and shall produce a non-tacky polished surface without colouring the leather unduly when tested as prescribed in Appendix B. 3.1.5 The polish shall be amenable to smooth spreading on the sole leather ancl edges of footwear and the rich transparent gloss shall appear on gentle rubbing with a brush or polishing cloth. 3.1.6 Flexibility - No visible cracks should be produced in the polish film when a piece of sole leather about 150 X 25 X 3 mm polished with the sample on buffed grain side, and after drying and finishing is bent round a mandrel of 25 mm diameter. 3.2 Keeping Quality - The material shall retain its consistency and shall comply with the requirements of this specification for one year from the date of actual delivery when stored in its original sealed containers at atmospheric temperature ( 21" to 38�C ). 3.3 The material Table 1. 4. APPENDIX B ( Clause 3.1.4 )
DETERMINATION B-l. PROCEDURE colour as and matt OF APPLICABILITY AND DRYING TIME

B-l.1 Sole leather pieces of the size 150 X 150 mm of the same the polish shall be used for testing. The piece shall be smooth finished ( non-glossy ) on the grain side. B-l.2 After the piece is buffed smooth on the surface with a cloth or brush to remove Apply the polish in a thin film to the smooth or brush and examine after two minutes in B-1.2.1 and B-1.2.2.

grain side, clean the grain any adhering dust particles. grain surface using a rag for the qualities described

B-1.2.1 Applicability - The leather piece to which the polish has been applied is polished after a minimum period of two minutes with a brush or soft cloth and examined for gloss visually. In case an approved sample of the polish is available, polish a similar piece of leather and match the gloss obtained with the test sample with that of the approved sample. B-1.2.2 Drying Time or Tack Free Condition - Take a leather piece coated with a thin film of polish (see B-1.2). Place the piece in one pan of a suitable physical balance and counterpoise it with weights. Place an additional weight of 2.5 kg and press the polished surface with the thumb till the two pans of the balance are counterpoised. Keep the thumb in this position for one minute and then slowly release. B-1.2.2.1 There shall be no sign of stickiness to the thumb. The thumb impression, if produced, shall be such that it shall be wiped out with a cloth or brush. 6

DETERMINATION C-l. PROCEDURE OF NON-VOLATILE MATTER

C-l.1 Weigh accurately about 3 g of the material as quickly as possible in a tared flat-bottomed dish of approximately 8 cm diameter provided :vith a cover. Heat without the cover on a steam-bath, for about 4 hours and then in an air-oven at 110" to 120�C for 16 hours. Cool and weigh. Simultaneously prepare non-volatile residue by the same procedure from about 40 g of the sample for further tests.

iv ) ] EXTRACT

OF pH OF WATER

F-l.1 Procedure - Add about 15 g of the material to 100 ml of distilled water in a beaker. Heat with stirring till all the wax has melted. Allow to cool to a temperature of 27 & 2�C. Separate the the aqueous layer from the wax cake and determine its PH using a PH-meter with a glass electrode in accordance with IS : 5741-1!370*.

J-l.8 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature the material does not vary unduly From the normal temperature. J-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING of

J-2.0 Samples to determine the conformity of a consignment of sole and edge wax polishes to this specification shall be selected so as to be representative of the consignment. Samples drawn in compliance with an agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, to evaluate the various characteristics of the polish, shall be held to be representative of the consignment. In case of dispute, the following sampling inspection scheme is recommended to serve as a guide. J-2.1 Lot -- All the containers in a single consignment of the material drawn from the sa.me batch of manufacture and belonging to the same size shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared or known to consist of different batches of manufacture or of different sizes of containers, the containers belonging to the same batch and size shall be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. J-2.1.1 Samples shall be tested for each lot for ascertaining formity of the material to the requirements of the specification. J-2.2 The upon the Table 2. the con-

J-2.2.1 In addition to the number of containers chosen in J-2.2, a number of containers shall be selected from each lot so as to determine consistency and to obtain 400.g of the material for determination of the distillation yield and flash pomt of the volatile portion of the material. J-2.3 These containers shall be chosen at random from the lot; in order to ensure the randomness of selection, some random number table as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier shall be used. In ca6e such table is not available, the following procedure shall be adopted. J-2.3.1 Arrange all the containers in the lot in a systematic manner and starting from any container, count them as I, 2, 3 ,... . . . . . etc, up to Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn from r and so on. the lot to give a sample for test, where r T-=.N/n, N being the total number of containers in the lot and n the number of containers to be chosen ( see In case r comes out to be a fractional number, its value shall Table 2 ). be taken to be equal to the integral part of it.
